caveats: Sample size depends on the precision target. n=100 is sized for a roughly +/-0.10 half-width at p=0.5; smaller half-widths require larger n.
claims.text: n=30 yields a 95% Wilson half-width of about 0.18 at p=0.5. That is too imprecise to publish a single FP-rate number from. Recommend committing to n=100 for the headline estimate and using n=30 only as a fast first pass to validate the rubric.

Without an off-cluster Tier B comparator, the labels measure within-cluster FP rate only and cannot distinguish 'the cluster is a real over-refusal hotspot' from 'the model over-refuses everywhere on this distribution'. Recommend stratified sampling (Tier A: 50 in-cluster, Tier B: 50 off-cluster).

The pre-registered distinguishability rule uses the 95% CI on the A-minus-B difference (Newcombe hybrid score), not overlap of the two tier CIs. CI overlap is a conservative and unreliable substitute for a difference test.

The rubric explicitly carves out hedged refusal (HR) as a separate class from compliance (C) and full refusal (FR). Collapsing HR into C or FR is the most common labeling shortcut and is the load-bearing rubric decision.
